note: Offline fixtures for the four non-image service paths. Nothing here contacts a network, and no brief names an Amazon host: the bulksheet is a file the seller already downloaded, the Golden Goose candidates are rows the seller's buyer typed in, the research corpus is a local document set, and each listing brief is the product facts the seller has plus a recorded model answer, so the app's own deterministic normalisation is exercised without a paid call. Five briefs per path at minimum, each one a different situation with its own constraints, ordered from ordinary to awkward.

listing.why: the path calls bojo_tools.publishing.compose_listing -> reasoning_tasks.listing_proposal; ty/services.json gives listingforge the compose_listing tool and calls it ListingForge copy

ppc.why: upload -> proposal -> approve -> write -> download are the /api/design-studio/amazon-files/* endpoints in design_studio_api.py, and the surface is Design Studio -> Ads -> Amazon files (northstar-os-ui/src/pages/internal/design-studio/AmazonFiles.jsx). AdPilot only reads the imported bulksheets, so it is not the producer of this artefact.
ppc.never_blended: design-studio's published seller score comes from the image pass. These rows are a separate population and are reported, never averaged with it.

golden_goose.why: the path calls bojo_tools.sourcing.golden_goose_scan, which is the golden_goose_scan tool. ty/services.json declares that same tool, and the same purpose text, for both 'goldengoose' and 'golden-goose', so the two ids are one product under two names rather than two services.
golden_goose.alias_note: the alias is declared here, not inferred: it adds no brief and no sample, it reuses the one sample the registry's own duplicate id describes.

research.why: no service in ty/services.json declares a path that reaches research_graph.research: the module is exercised by its own test only, and nothing in the registry or the backend calls it. The pass is measured and reported, but attributing it to product-finder (or anything else) would be inventing an owner.
